Monday, September 7, 2026 Daily Digest

"The Marketing Stack Is Dead," 96% Use AI But Hiring Shifts to Judgment, 6sense Routes Intent to AI Agents

Today's top stories in AI + enterprise tech

1

Totaligent: "The Marketing Stack Is Dead. AI Wrote the Obituary."

A new white paper delivers the harshest verdict yet on martech sprawl: 15,500+ products, utilization near 50%, and martech's share of marketing budgets at a multi-year low — even as paid media spend rose. The argument: enterprise marketing is resetting from a "rented stack of disconnected tools" to a unified communications operating system. The implications for enterprise software vendors: platform consolidation is no longer optional.

Read on GlobeNewswire →
2

96% of B2B Marketers Use AI, But Hiring Is Shifting to Judgment Roles

Three separate 2026 research releases converge on the same reality: the AI tool rollout is largely done; the hard part is now governance, data plumbing, and talent design. HubSpot finds 80% of marketers use AI to create content, while Demand Gen Report puts adoption at 96%. But the hiring shift is toward QA, judgment, and orchestration — not more prompt engineers. The efficiency lever (45% cite it as top benefit) is real, but so is the skills gap.

Read on MarketScale →
3

6sense Routes B2B Intent Data Directly to AI Agents

6sense launched product updates that pipe revenue data — B2B intent signals, account stages, buying predictions — directly into external AI agents like Claude, ChatGPT, and Agentforce. This is the "agents reading your CRM" vision going live: AI systems now consume intent data natively, not through dashboards. The enterprise implication: data infrastructure that can serve AI agents is becoming table stakes.

Read on MarTech →
4

Sitefire (YC W26): Marketing to AI Agents, Not Humans

Y Combinator's Winter '26 batch includes Sitefire, a startup that helps brands market their products to AI agents. The thesis: as ChatGPT, Claude, and other AI assistants become discovery surfaces, brands need content and structured data that AI agents can parse. Sitefire identifies which content drives AI visibility and auto-generates it. It's the first real "AI SEO" play — and a signal that enterprise content strategy may soon have two audiences.

View on YC →
5

Meta's AI Agent "Hatch" Launches Inside WhatsApp and Instagram

Following its $18B settlement, Meta is reportedly releasing Hatch, a consumer AI agent that runs inside WhatsApp and Instagram. The agent can perform autonomous tasks including online purchases and restaurant bookings. For enterprise software, this is the B2C version of what 6sense is doing for B2B: AI agents making decisions on behalf of users. The implication: enterprise messaging and commerce APIs may need to serve agents, not just humans.

Read on CNBC →

💡 My Take

Read this one: The MarketScale piece on AI adoption vs. data/talent readiness. The stat that jumps out: 96% adoption, but the hiring shift is toward judgment roles — QA, orchestration, governance. This is the real 2026 story. Tool rollout is done. The moat is now human oversight of AI systems, not more AI tools. Enterprise leaders who can audit, validate, and govern AI outputs will have leverage.
